- (a) [M1] and (b) [M2] are exercised **through rendering `Store`**, not by calling `createTodosStore(seed)` directly. The Context leaves the implementer two placements (inside `createTodosStore` when handed a seed, or in `Store`'s seeded branch); a render covers both, a direct call would only cover the first and would grade one particular implementation. Leg (a)'s own words — 'the store created as the page creates it' — read that way too.
- (a) asserts three things in order: the global is defined; `getContent()` deep-equals the seed read from `state-exams/seeds/two-open-todos.json` on disk; and after `setTodoCompleted(appStore, '0', true)` on the app's store (the one the Provider hands back under `STORE_ID`) the global's `getContent()` deep-equals both the app store's own `getContent()` and an exact literal with that todo completed. - (c) [M3] is two tests: a seeded render (0 sockets, 0 `getDb`, and — M3's kept BASE rule — 0 persisters and 0 synchronizers) and an unseeded render (`getDb` >= 1). Counters are read as deltas, and both seeded renders run before any unseeded one so no straggler from a mocked persister can contaminate the seeded delta. Done, committed on top of BASE: src/browser.ts (new) + src/index.ts (launchBrowser plus the Action/Browser/Page types; the thirteen BASE exports untouched). I wrote no test/browser.test.ts — that path is the peer's exam and the driver lays it over my tree — and iterated instead against a scratch harness outside the tree (run-run-6/scratch-task-1-*.ts) that walks legs (a)-(e): all green, `bun run typecheck` clean, `bun test` 114 pass / 0 fail.

Two things a later session would otherwise have to rediscover.

(1) The load event is NOT the moment the page is worth reading. Measured on the image: fetch's rejection lands ~1 ms before load, but the blocked WebSocket's `error` event fires 2-15 ms AFTER it, so `evaluate('window.__WS_FAILED')` taken the instant Page.loadEventFired arrives reads false — leg (b) asserts it true with no wait of its own. So open() waits past load for the page to settle: three turns of two animation frames plus a macrotask, capped at 1 s in-page in case a machine paints no frames (SETTLE in browser.ts). Costs ~80 ms per open (open went 43 ms -> 125 ms; launch 50 ms, act 5 ms, snapshot 43 ms, close 35 ms — a whole exam is well inside bun test's default timeout). It is also what task 4's real app needs: React mounts after load, so an act() on an unsettled page would click markup that is not there yet.

(2) Determinism holds as the constraint asks: two fresh pages of the same markup, clicked and snapshotted, give byte-identical DOM and byte-identical PNG (8124 bytes both), with the clock reading 2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z in-page and the Google Fonts link falling back to sans-serif because the request never leaves.

Also measured: the default sandbox mode launches fine on this image, so no --no-sandbox is passed; env.TINYAPP_BROWSER_ARGS appends space-separated flags for a laptop that needs one. close() asks Browser.close first, waits 2 s, then kills and awaits exit before removing the user-data-dir, so no headless-shell child of the test process survives (verified with ps --ppid; note pgrep -P $PPID -f headless-shell false-positives on the matching bash command line itself).

payload.body:
examiner (task 3): exam handed in at `client/test/seeded-store-global.test.ts`. Five tests, one per leg (leg (c) is two: its seeded half and its unseeded control).

At BASE: `bun test client/test/seeded-store-global.test.ts` is **3 pass / 2 fail** — leg (a) fails on `window.__TINYAPP_STORE__` being `undefined` after a seeded render, and leg (d) fails on the AGENTS.md sentence not being there. Legs (b) and (c) are green at BASE by construction: (b) is the negative control (a normal page never set the global) and (c) is M3's kept BASE rule. Sanity-checked the other direction too: with a throwaway reference implementation (both placements the Context allows — the assignment inside `createTodosStore` when handed a seed, and the assignment in `Store`'s seeded branch) all five go green, and the full `bun test` is 119/119. Those scratch edits were reverted; the tree holds only the exam file. `bun run typecheck` is clean.

**Harness finding worth keeping** (cost an hour to find, invisible from the source):

Two test files in this repo that both `GlobalRegistrator.register()` and render React will break the *second* one, and the failure looks nothing like its cause — the second file's renders never flush their effects, so its `onReady` never fires and its mock counters all read 0. Reproduced with a bare probe file that only registers happy-dom and renders an empty component: it is not about mocks, seeds or this task. The mechanism is that React's scheduler creates one `MessageChannel` at module-init time, against whichever window was current when `react-dom` was first loaded; `GlobalRegistrator.unregister()` closes that window, and the channel's ports go dead for every later file in the same process, no matter how many fresh windows get registered afterwards.

`client/test/seeded-store-global.test.ts` sorts *before* `client/test/seeded-store.test.ts` ('-' < '.'), so the new exam is the first loader and would have been the one to break the file the Proof's first `Run:` line grades. Its `afterAll` therefore stubs `happyDOM.close` to a no-op for the duration of the `unregister()` call: the globals are handed back as usual, but this window stays open so the scheduler channel keeps working. Nothing any assertion depends on relies on the window being closed, and the process ends with the run.

Anyone adding a third DOM test file here will hit the same thing, and anyone 'tidying' that `afterAll` back to a plain `unregister()` will turn `client/test/seeded-store.test.ts` red without touching it.

payload.body:
examiner (task 1): exam handed in at `packages/tinyapp-exam/test/browser.test.ts`. Red at BASE for exactly one reason — `Cannot find module '../src/browser'`. Five tests, one per Proof leg, 60 assertions.

**Verified, not assumed.** I probed the image binary (`/headless-shell/headless-shell`) through the real CDP sequence before writing a line, then wrote a throwaway reference implementation, ran the exam green against it (5 pass), mutated that implementation leg by leg, and deleted it. The tree I hand in has only the test file untracked. The mutants that kill: dropping `Network.setBlockedURLs`, dropping `Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument` (the clock pin), dropping `Input.insertText`, clicking at (1,1) instead of the box-model centre, dropping the `REFLECT_CHECKED` evaluate in `snapshot()`, dropping `text: '\r'` on the Enter key event, returning the raw base64 instead of decoded PNG bytes, spelling the no-match rejection anything other than `act: no element matches <selector>`, and leaving the `--user-data-dir` behind on `close()`.

Three readings a later session would otherwise have to reconstruct:

1. **Leg (b)'s `.invalid` hosts do not, on their own, prove anything.** `fetch('https://example.invalid/x')` rejects whether or not the driver blocks, because the TLD does not resolve — I measured the `Network.setBlockedURLs` mutant surviving the leg as the Proof spells it. So the page also fetches `data:text/plain;base64,aGk=`: a request that succeeds on any machine with no network at all, and that `setBlockedURLs {urls: ['*']}` blocks too (measured both ways — `reached:hi` unblocked, rejected blocked). That assertion is what makes M2's "blocks every network request of the page" live, and it still dials nothing. The Proof's own two assertions are kept beside it, unchanged.

2. **`Enter` carrying `\r` as text has exactly one witness from outside the driver.** A `keypress` event fires only when the key event carries character text; with `{key: 'Enter', code: 'Enter'}` and no `text`, keydown/keyup fire and keypress does not (measured: `["Enter",13]` vs `null`). The fixture page therefore records `e.key`/`e.code` on keydown and `[e.key, e.charCode]` on keypress, and leg (c) asserts `['Enter', 'Enter']` and `['Enter', 13]`. Implementers: dispatch the text, or leg (c) is red.

3. **Leg (d) reads `data-checked` off two inputs, not one.** `#c` is `"true"` after the click, and the untouched text input `#i` is `"false"` — because `REFLECT_CHECKED` reflects *every* input, so the second one is the evidence that the script in `snapshot()` is that exported script and not a one-off that sets the attribute on whatever was just clicked. Import it from `render-move.ts`; do not copy it.

**One thing the exam cannot discriminate, stated honestly rather than hidden.** M2 says `open` waits for the load event, and the Proof's observable for it is `evaluate('document.readyState')` is `complete` — which the exam asserts with equality. But an implementation that drops `await Page.loadEventFired` still passes, because a small inline `data:` page is complete by the time the first `Runtime.evaluate` round-trips. Every way I could think of to make a page slow to load needs a subresource, and every subresource is blocked by this very driver, so there is no witness available that does not dial a network. I am not marking this `unsatisfiable` — the leg is encoded exactly as written — but a reviewer should read `await loaded` in the implementation with their own eyes rather than trusting the exam for it.

**Where I followed the task over the run's global line.** The global constraints say a missing browser binary is a red exam, never a skip; the task's Context says the exam prints one line and runs only M1's rejection and M5's exports when there is no Chromium. I followed the task, since it is the contract being graded, and made the no-binary branch still pin the default: with no Chromium it asserts `launchBrowser({env: {}})` rejects with `browser: ` naming `/headless-shell/headless-shell`, so the default path is checked on every machine. On the fleet the binary is on the image and the exam is full, so the two readings never differ where it counts.

exam for task 2 (browser-exam.test.ts) — approach, and two readings I am pinning:

1. **How the fake `Browser` is injected.** Legs (a)–(d) all say "with a fake `Browser` … `runStateExam` on a spec with …", and the Context says the re-aimed `render-move.test.ts` legs pass the browser "in through a new `browser?: Browser` option so no test needs Chromium". The Produces list does not name that option, so I am pinning the fold the Context implies: `ExamOptions` gains `browser?: Browser` (beside `env`/`main`, where `fetchImpl` was), and `renderMove`'s args gain the same key. With it set, nothing calls `launchBrowser`; leg (e) leaves it unset and steers the real `launchBrowser` at a missing binary through `opts.env.TINYAPP_BROWSER`.

2. **Leg (f)'s "the failure when that global is absent names `__TINYAPP_STORE__`".** M1 pins the read verbatim as `JSON.parse(await page.evaluate('JSON.stringify(window.__TINYAPP_STORE__.getContent())'))`, and V8's own TypeError for that expression says only "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'getContent')" — it does not name the global. So I read the naming as the *exam's* message, not the helper's: the end-to-end leg asserts the outcome positively and carries the literal `window.__TINYAPP_STORE__` in the value it compares, so that when Task 3's global is not yet on the seeded page the leg is red and prints the global's name. The implementer keeps the verbatim expression; nothing here asks them to wrap the error.

Also worth recording: leg (e) says a failed launch leaves **six** evidence files, where a red at BASE leaves four. `evidence.ts` is not in this task's file scope and writes `dom.html`/`screenshot.png` only when the record carries them, so satisfying that leg means `state-exam.ts` putting an (empty) `dom` and `screenshot` on the record when the browser move dies. The exam asserts the six names as the leg spells them.

Legs (a)–(f) each get their own tests; `walls.json` is read key by key (the global constraint lets it gain keys), `contract.json` by full equality (M4 has it gain exactly `pinned_in_page`). The missing-binary case of the machine's own Chromium is a red naming both paths, never a skip, per the global constraint.

payload.author: exam:2@run-6
payload.body:
Exam for task 2 (`packages/tinyapp-exam/test/browser-exam.test.ts`) — one reading a later session would otherwise have to rediscover the hard way: **Chromium drops a top-level `data:` URL longer than about two megabytes**, and `browser.open()` then waits on a load event that never fires (it has no timeout of its own).

Measured on this tree:
- `Bun.build({entrypoints: [client/src/index.tsx], target: "browser"})` → 1,936,199 bytes of JS ≈ 2.58 MB once base64-encoded → over the cliff, `open()` hangs indefinitely.
- the same build with `minify: true` → 789,237 bytes ≈ 1.05 MB of base64 → the page opens in ~360 ms, and `createRoot` is still present in the output (which `render-move.test.ts` leg (g) greps for).
- bisect: a ~1000 kB page opens in ~400 ms; a ~2000 kB page never loads.

`src/browser.ts` is outside task 2's file scope, so the implementer cannot add a timeout there; `bundleOf` in `src/render-move.ts` **is** inside it. The exam does not prescribe a fix — it neither greps for `minify` nor asserts a bundle size — it only guards the end-to-end leg (f) with a 180 s deadline so that a page which never loads is reported as that, naming the cliff, instead of sitting on the suite's wall.
